title: The project connects three kinds of work
treatment: Integration workbench: contributions support shared agreements; the integrator stays accountable
status: Production complete; Sol native-frame, encoded-quality and course-playback checks passed.
learning_payoff: Different suppliers and open interfaces do not remove the integration work. Three complementary work areas support shared agreements, and contributions do not transfer complete-product responsibility.
caption: Tools and flows, ecosystem standards, and open interfaces support shared integration agreements. Contributions help the work; the integrator remains responsible for the complete product.
alt: Two supplier dies sit below shared integration agreements supported by tools, standards and interfaces. The integrator retains responsibility for the complete product.
reduced_motion: Use the final state at 42.8 seconds with the caption and unchanged transcript. It shows the same Compute and I/O supplier identities, shared agreements, the three supporting work areas, and complete-product responsibility. No motion is needed to understand the distinction.
spatial_grammar: Supplier A / Compute stays left; Supplier B / I/O stays right; their notched silhouettes persist.
Paper objects represent design information, expectations or contributions. They are not source-code exports, certificates or qualification results.
The only electrical channel is the line between die edges in the first explanatory view. The buying-example view is explicitly labelled and does not claim that the selected pair is compatible.
The open lower bracket is a responsibility scope, not a package outline or a whole-scene border.
Green marks current instructional emphasis; it never means approved, passed, secure or interchangeable.

scenes.spoken_cue: The Open Compute Project's Open Chiplet Economy project, or O C E, brings companies together around multi-vendor chiplet systems.
scenes.motion_and_reason: Two notched dies retain Supplier A/Compute and Supplier B/I/O identities. They move closer at 4.44–6.68 seconds but remain separate, above an open “System to integrate” scope. This represents collaboration around a product question, not an assembled or qualified product.

scenes.spoken_cue: Its work is broader than an electrical connection.
scenes.motion_and_reason: A neutral physical connection appears between the two die edges. An open scope above it expands beyond the channel at 8.32–9.60 seconds, making electrical communication one part of the wider task. No full-scene frame is drawn.

scenes.spoken_cue: Tools and flows help teams exchange design information.
scenes.motion_and_reason: A folded Design info paper travels from one supplier team to the other at 11.74–12.84 seconds, above the dies. This separates design-information exchange from the physical connection below. No source-code file, detailed proprietary model or exchange format is invented.
scenes.hold: 12.84–13.78: received information stays by Supplier B.

scenes.motion_and_reason: Two schematic expectation papers align to a shared reading baseline at 14.34–15.02 seconds. The dies stay fixed; the documents align, not mechanical contacts. The line joins the expectation view without a pass mark.

One highlight crosses the existing physical connection at 17.72–18.65 seconds. It illustrates the role of an interface; it is not a wire-level timing trace or proof of compatibility for this supplier pair.

scenes.spoken_cue: Imagine buying a compute die from one supplier and an input-output die from another.
scenes.motion_and_reason: Cut explicitly to “Illustrative supplier pair”. The same Compute die moves toward the integration area on its cue (20.38–21.44); the same I/O die follows on its cue (22.26–23.40). Supplier identities move with their supplied objects. An open lower scope is already labelled Integrator; no package or passing result is shown.
scenes.hold: 23.40–24.22: both supplied dies remain separate in the integration scope.

scenes.spoken_cue: Someone must still establish their package compatibility, test access, startup behavior, and commercial responsibilities.
scenes.motion_and_reason: Keep the pair unresolved and display the four short questions around it from the start of the sentence. Weight emphasis follows package compatibility at 25.62, test access at 26.88, startup behavior at 27.84 and commercial responsibilities at 28.94. The question mark remains; there are no checks, invented tests, startup mechanisms or automatic responsibility transfers.
scenes.hold: 29.34–30.56: four obligations and the pair remain visible.

scenes.spoken_cue: The project provides a place to develop those shared agreements.
scenes.motion_and_reason: A labelled regrouping cut collects the same four questions on a single folded working document. Dies remain visibly separate below it and the Integrator scope remains. The full list is unchanged and unapproved. A clean cut avoids text moving through the die silhouettes.
scenes.hold: 31.12–33.78: the working document and responsibilities hold.

scenes.spoken_cue: Participation can include reviewing a specification, supplying a model, or testing an implementation.
scenes.motion_and_reason: Reframe to a compact Shared agreements paper above the same dies. A Review note joins from the left at 35.00–35.95; a Model note joins from the right at 36.42–37.25; a Test note joins from the left at 37.72–38.60. Each slides under the working paper; offset sheet edges preserve accumulated contributions without counts or approval stamps. The Integrator scope never leaves.
visible_labels: Review a specification / Supply a model / Test an implementation
scenes.hold: 38.60–39.32: contribution sheets hold; no product result appears.

scenes.spoken_cue: No single contribution removes the integrator's responsibility for the complete product.
scenes.motion_and_reason: Establish the final summary immediately and hold it unchanged: tools/flows, standards and interfaces feed shared agreements; the same supplied Compute and I/O dies sit below; the open lower scope explicitly names complete-product responsibility. This is a static conclusion, not certification or automatic integration.

sources.scope: Authoritative teaching scope, illustrative compute/I/O purchase, four integration obligations, contribution examples and explicit integrator accountability.

sources.section: Optimizing Silicon for AI — Open Chiplet Economy
sources.scope: Multiple ownership layers and the complete open-system outcome; supports broad integration scope. The explicit integrator responsibility wording comes from the locked script.
Open collaboration and standardization for multi-vendor systems; EDA tools/flows exchange design data and models; ecosystem standards define architecture; open interfaces connect chiplets.
Interoperability remains to be demonstrated/verifiable and the contract between chiplets requires work. Used as a limit, not a claim that any illustrated pair is qualified.
Business relationships, project structures and model agreements address commercial barriers. Does not define the legal content or transfer responsibility.
Contribute to workstreams, meetings/feedback, implement specifications and ask suppliers to build to them. Specific model/testing examples are in the approved script.
Local supporting transcript for work areas and participation. No audible verification or new retrieval.

source_note: Actual PDF viewer pages 2, 3, 8, 9 and 11 were verified against summit-01.pdf. The existing course also links the OCE project page; no cached copy was found and no fresh retrieval was needed for this script-level treatment.
technical_limits: No certification, universal interchangeability, source-code sharing, approved complete product, automatic responsibility transfer or invented legal obligation.
No actual package construction, interface protocol, startup state machine, test access architecture or quantitative result.
The four topics remain work to establish. Shared agreements and contribution sheets do not become an approval checklist.
Supplier labels identify the illustrative origin of each die; movement is conceptual acquisition/integration, not a prescribed manufacturing flow.
No backward-version references, year/edition badges, course branding, slide-title duplication, source footer or enclosing decorative frame in the media.

implementation.timeline: One deterministic silent pass; no loops, fades, hidden state, audio or runtime randomness.
implementation.encoding: Sol owns final silent 2560×1440 H.264 encoding and integration.

self_review.contained_text_font_metrics: Bundled Open Sans variable font set to weight 600 / width 100; measured minimum clearance exceeds 0.75em for smallest Compute die and all moving document labels.
self_review.native_frame_visual_qa: Accepted by Sol: native/displayed-size and transition-adjacent samples, final decode at200%, desktop/phone and real paired-media controls.

approval_checklist: Check native and displayed-size keyframes, plus transition-adjacent frames and a complete muted pass.

Keep the ending held; pair identity and complete-product accountability must remain readable.
Preserve final WAV/script hashes and use exact WAV duration within one encoded frame.
Confirm synchronized pause/seek/speed/end/replay and reduced-motion behavior in the real course.
